three metal-controlled protein dimer designs based on the β1 domain were successfully created.

three metal-controlled protein complexes were designed and characterized that adopt the target structure in the dimeric state and are fully monomeric and monodisperse without metal.

developing a new class of protein complexes with high affinity, high stability, and the ability to be regulated with a metal-ligand interaction.
the design of high-affinity protein dimers that form and dissociate in response to the presence of metal ions, providing a new platform for biomaterial design.
the design of high-affinity, metal-controlled protein dimmers that are monomeric and completely inactive in the absence of zinc and dimeric and fully functional in its presence.

the designed proteins represent a promising new approach to the design of metal-controlled protein complexes.

we designed three protein dimers that bind metal and form high-affinity dimmers in the presence of ZnSO4.
we have designed a series of three high-affinity metal-controlled protein dimmers.
we have successfully designed three high-affinity metal-controlled dimers that can form in the presence of divalent metal ions and dissociate upon addition EDTA.

the β1 domain is an excellent scaffold for the design of metal-controlled protein dimeric systems.
it is possible to design high-affinity metal-controlled protein dimer systems with a relatively small number of mutations.
